about.title: About MaternalCare
about.intro: MaternalCare was designed to make pregnancy care coordinated, measurable, and deeply respectful. We believe that mothers should be in control of their care journey, and partners should have practical, meaningful ways to support them — rooted in the warmth and wisdom of Indian family traditions.
about.philosophy1: Pregnancy is a profound life transition — celebrated across Indian culture as a sacred journey. It requires physical care, emotional support, practical coordination, and informed decision-making. Yet too often, the systems designed to help either treat the mother as a passive patient or become tools of surveillance rather than support.
about.philosophy2: We built MaternalCare differently — drawing inspiration from the mandala, an ancient Indian symbol of wholeness and harmony. Our platform puts the mother at the center — not as a subject to be monitored, but as an autonomous person navigating a complex journey. Partners are engaged as allies, not overseers. Every design decision starts from the question: Does this respect the mother's autonomy?
about.principle1Desc: Nothing is shared without the mother's explicit consent. She controls visibility at all times.
about.principle2Desc: We use rule-based nudges and trackable support actions — not monitoring or passive tracking.
about.principle3Desc: Clear disclaimers, emergency escalation, and guardrails. We never diagnose or prescribe.
about.principle4Desc: Every interaction is designed for calm, clarity, and reduced cognitive load during a demanding time.
about.not1: A medical device or diagnostic tool
about.not2: A replacement for clinical care or professional advice
about.not3: A surveillance system for partners to monitor mothers
about.not4: A social network or community forum
about.footerDisclaimer: This platform supports pregnancy care but does not provide medical diagnosis, treatment, or replace professional healthcare.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about MaternalCare, privacy, features, and safety.
faq.cat1Q1: How do I create an account?
faq.cat1A1: Click "Get Started" on the home page and fill in your basic information. You will be guided through a simple onboarding flow where you can set your pregnancy profile and preferences.
faq.cat1Q2: Can I use MaternalCare without a partner?
faq.cat1A2: Yes. The mother dashboard works independently. You can track your pregnancy, log symptoms, set reminders, and access weekly guidance without linking a partner account.
faq.cat1A3: From your settings, you can invite a partner by email. They will receive an invitation to create their own account linked to your family. You control what they can see.
faq.cat2Q1: What does my partner see by default?
faq.cat2A1: Nothing. By default, all your data is private. You must explicitly choose which items to share. You can change visibility at any time from the share toggle on each entry.
faq.cat2Q2: Can I hide something after sharing it?
faq.cat2A2: Yes. You can revoke shared visibility at any time. The item immediately becomes private to you only.
faq.cat2Q3: Is my health data stored securely?
faq.cat2A3: All data is encrypted at rest and in transit. We use industry-standard security practices including hashed passwords, input validation, rate limiting, and audit logging.
faq.cat3Q1: How is the pregnancy week calculated?
faq.cat3A1: You can set your pregnancy basis as LMP (last menstrual period) or due date. The system calculates your current week and provides week-specific guidance, milestones, and tips.
faq.cat3Q2: Does the chatbot give medical advice?
faq.cat3A2: No. The chatbot provides navigation help, reminder prompts, and general guidance from curated content. It never diagnoses or prescribes. If you mention emergency warning signs, it immediately directs you to seek clinical care.
faq.cat3Q3: What are the support actions for partners?
faq.cat3A3: Partners receive daily micro-tasks like confirming transport for appointments, preparing meals, or checking in emotionally. These are practical, concrete actions — not passive tips.
faq.cat3A4: Currently, each account supports one active pregnancy profile at a time. You can update or reset your profile if needed.
faq.cat4Q1: What happens if I report an emergency symptom?
faq.cat4A1: The system immediately shows emergency escalation guidance and directs you to seek clinical care. It does not continue casual conversation or attempt to diagnose.
faq.cat4A2: No. MaternalCare is a pregnancy coordination and support platform. It is not a medical device, diagnostic tool, or replacement for professional healthcare.
faq.cat4Q3: Who can I contact for help?
faq.cat4A3: If you have questions about using the platform, use the chatbot or check the FAQ. For medical concerns, always contact your healthcare provider.
faq.ctaSubtitle: Our chatbot assistant can help you find answers and navigate the platform.
faq.footerDisclaimer: This platform supports pregnancy care but does not provide medical diagnosis or treatment.

factsAndMyths.heroSubtitle: Separating traditional beliefs from medical evidence. Verified information tailored for Indian mothers-to-be.
factsAndMyths.mythsDisclaimer: These myths are widely believed across Indian households. Each one is debunked with medical facts.
factsAndMyths.myth1Myth: Eating saffron (kesar) during pregnancy makes the baby fair-skinned.
factsAndMyths.myth1Fact: Skin color is determined by genetics, not diet. Saffron in moderation may aid digestion but does not affect complexion. Excessive saffron can even trigger uterine contractions — consult your doctor before using it.
factsAndMyths.myth2Myth: Pregnant women should eat for two — double the portions.
factsAndMyths.myth2Fact: You only need about 300 extra calories per day in the second trimester and 450 in the third. Quality matters more than quantity — focus on nutrient-dense foods like leafy greens, lentils, dairy, and fruits.
factsAndMyths.myth3Myth: Avoid papaya and pineapple — they cause miscarriage.
factsAndMyths.myth3Fact: Only raw/unripe papaya contains latex that may trigger contractions. Ripe papaya is safe in moderation. Pineapple contains bromelain but you would need to eat 7–10 whole pineapples for any effect. Both are safe in normal dietary amounts.
factsAndMyths.myth4Myth: You should not exercise or do yoga during pregnancy.
factsAndMyths.myth4Fact: Moderate exercise and prenatal yoga are recommended by WHO and AYUSH Ministry. They reduce back pain, improve sleep, and may ease labor. Always consult your doctor and avoid high-impact activities.
factsAndMyths.myth5Myth: Drinking ghee in the last trimester ensures a smooth delivery.
factsAndMyths.myth5Fact: There is no scientific evidence that ghee consumption eases delivery. While healthy fats are important, excess ghee can lead to unnecessary weight gain and gestational diabetes risk. A balanced diet is key.
factsAndMyths.myth6Myth: Avoid going out during eclipses — it harms the baby.
factsAndMyths.myth6Fact: There is no scientific basis for this belief. Eclipses are astronomical events with no proven effect on fetal development. Staying indoors is a cultural practice, not a medical necessity.
factsAndMyths.myth7Myth: Spicy food causes heartburn and harms the baby.
factsAndMyths.myth7Fact: While spicy food may worsen heartburn/acid reflux (common in pregnancy), it does not harm the baby. If you tolerate spice well, moderate consumption is safe. Listen to your body.
factsAndMyths.myth8Myth: Climbing stairs or reaching up high can cause the umbilical cord to wrap around the baby’s neck.
factsAndMyths.myth8Fact: Nuchal cord (cord around the neck) occurs in about 1 in 3 births and is related to fetal movement, not maternal activity. Normal daily movements are safe. Avoid overexertion as per your doctor’s advice.
factsAndMyths.myth9Myth: Drinking coconut water makes the baby’s head bigger or causes cold.
factsAndMyths.myth9Fact: Coconut water is actually excellent during pregnancy — it is rich in electrolytes, prevents dehydration, and helps with urinary tract health. It does not cause cold or affect head size. Drink it fresh and in moderation.
factsAndMyths.myth10Myth: You must deliver at exactly 9 months — crossing the due date is dangerous.
factsAndMyths.myth10Fact: A full-term pregnancy is 39–40 weeks. Only about 5% of babies are born on their exact due date. Delivering up to 42 weeks can be normal under medical supervision. Your doctor will monitor and decide if induction is needed.
factsAndMyths.fact1Desc: The Government of India recommends 400 mcg of folic acid daily from preconception through the first trimester to prevent neural tube defects. IFA (Iron Folic Acid) tablets are provided free at all government health centers under the Anemia Mukt Bharat program.
factsAndMyths.fact2Desc: Two doses of Tetanus Toxoid (TT) injection are recommended during pregnancy as per India’s Universal Immunization Programme. The first dose in early pregnancy and second at least 4 weeks later. This protects both mother and newborn from tetanus.
factsAndMyths.fact3Desc: WHO and MoHFW recommend at least 4 Antenatal Care visits during pregnancy: 1st within 12 weeks, 2nd at 20–24 weeks, 3rd at 28–32 weeks, and 4th at 36–38 weeks. High-risk pregnancies may need more frequent monitoring.
factsAndMyths.fact4Desc: Iodine deficiency during pregnancy is a leading cause of preventable intellectual disability. India’s Universal Salt Iodization program ensures iodized salt reaches all households. Always use iodized salt — it is mandatory under FSSAI regulations.
factsAndMyths.fact5Desc: Over 50% of pregnant women in India are anemic. Take your prescribed IFA tablets daily. Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C (like lemon on dal) for better absorption. Avoid tea/coffee immediately after meals as tannins block iron absorption.
factsAndMyths.fact6Desc: Pregnant women need 1000–1200 mg of calcium daily. Calcium supplementation reduces the risk of pre-eclampsia and preterm birth. Dairy, ragi (finger millet), sesame seeds (til), and green leafy vegetables are excellent sources in the Indian diet.
factsAndMyths.fact7Desc: WHO and GoI recommend initiating breastfeeding within the first hour of birth. The first milk (colostrum) is rich in antibodies and must NOT be discarded — this is a common harmful practice in parts of India. Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months is the national recommendation.
factsAndMyths.fact8Desc: For low birth weight babies, Kangaroo Mother Care (skin-to-skin contact with the mother) is recommended by WHO. It stabilizes heart rate, breathing, and temperature, and promotes breastfeeding. India has adopted KMC as a national strategy in SNCUs across districts.
factsAndMyths.ctaTitle: Ready to Start Your Pregnancy Journey?
factsAndMyths.ctaSubtitle: Join thousands of Indian mothers who trust Maa Care for personalized, evidence-based pregnancy support.
factsAndMyths.safetyText: This information is educational and based on WHO, MoHFW (Government of India), and ICMR guidelines. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your doctor or healthcare provider for personalized guidance during pregnancy.

privacy.section1P1: MaternalCare is built on the principle that you should always be in control of your personal health information. We designed this platform to facilitate coordination between mothers and their support circles while ensuring that sensitive data is never shared without explicit, informed consent.
privacy.section1P2: This privacy policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, who can access it, and what rights you have over your information. We encourage you to read it carefully before using the platform.
privacy.section2_1Desc: When you create an account, we collect your first name, last name, email address or phone number, and a hashed password. If you register as a mother, you may optionally provide your date of birth and pregnancy-related dates (last menstrual period or estimated due date) to enable week-by-week tracking.
privacy.section2_2Desc: If you are a mother, you may choose to log symptoms, mood entries, wellness activities, and appointment records. This data is stored securely and is only visible to you by default. You may choose to share specific categories of this data with linked support partners through the platform's sharing controls.
privacy.section2_3Desc: Messages sent to the in-platform chatbot are processed to provide relevant responses. Chat history is stored to maintain conversation context, but is not shared with any third party. Emergency-related conversations are flagged for safety but not shared without your consent.
privacy.section2_4Desc: Like most web platforms, we collect standard technical information including your IP address, browser type, device information, and interaction logs. This data is used for security monitoring, debugging, and improving the platform experience.
privacy.section3Item1: To provide and personalise the MaternalCare experience for you
privacy.section3Item2: To enable coordination features between you and your linked support partners
privacy.section3Item3: To generate week-by-week pregnancy guidance based on your due date
privacy.section3Item4: To send notifications and reminders based on your preferences
privacy.section3Item5: To detect emergency situations and provide appropriate safety guidance
privacy.section3Item6: To improve the platform through aggregated, anonymised usage analytics
privacy.section3Item7: To comply with legal obligations and enforce our terms of service
privacy.section4_1Desc: MaternalCare is designed with a privacy-first architecture. By default, all your personal and health data is private to you. You can granularly control what categories of information are shared with your linked support partners through the Settings page. You can revoke sharing permissions at any time, and previously shared data will no longer be visible to the partner.
privacy.section4_2Title: 4.2 We Do Not Sell Your Data
privacy.section4_2Desc: We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal or health data to any third party — ever. This includes advertisers, data brokers, insurance companies, and research organisations. Your data is used solely to provide the MaternalCare service to you.
privacy.section4_3Desc: We may disclose information if required by law, court order, or governmental regulation. We will make reasonable efforts to notify you before such disclosure, unless prohibited by law.
privacy.section5Intro: We implement industry-standard security measures to protect your data. This includes:
privacy.section5Item1: Passwords are hashed using bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds
privacy.section5Item2: All data transmission occurs over HTTPS/TLS encryption
privacy.section5Item3: Database access is restricted to authorised services only
privacy.section5Item4: Authentication tokens expire and are stored securely
privacy.section5Item5: Regular security audits and dependency updates
privacy.section5Disclaimer: However, no method of electronic storage or transmission is 100% secure. We cannot guarantee absolute security, but we are committed to maintaining a high standard of protection.
privacy.section6P1: We retain your data for as long as your account is active. If you choose to delete your account, all personally identifiable information will be permanently deleted within 30 days. Anonymised, aggregated data may be retained for platform improvement purposes and cannot be linked back to you.
privacy.section6P2: You can request a copy of your data or request account deletion at any time by contacting us through the Settings page or via email.
privacy.section7P1: MaternalCare is intended for use by adults aged 18 and above. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If we become aware that a child under 13 has provided us with personal data, we will take steps to delete such information promptly.
privacy.section8Intro: Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have the following rights regarding your personal data:
privacy.rightAccessDesc: Request a copy of the personal data we hold about you
privacy.rightRectificationDesc: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data
privacy.rightErasureDesc: Request deletion of your personal data (right to be forgotten)
privacy.rightRestrictionDesc: Request limitation of how we process your data
privacy.rightPortabilityDesc: Receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format
privacy.rightObjectionDesc: Object to certain types of data processing
privacy.section9P1: We may update this privacy policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices or legal requirements. We will notify you of any material changes through the platform or via email. Continued use of the platform after such changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
privacy.section10P1: If you have questions, concerns, or requests regarding this privacy policy or your personal data, please reach out through the in-platform support channels or contact our data protection team at the email address listed in your account settings.
privacy.section10Status: We respond to all inquiries within 48 hours
privacy.footerDisclaimer: This platform provides informational and coordination support only. It is not a medical device and does not provide medical diagnosis or treatment. Always consult with your healthcare provider for medical concerns.
